notes: Baseline calibration target. Source: 3-10 %/yr is the range conventionally quoted for cortical bone (Parfitt 2002, PMID 12052445); the 5-10 %/yr target used here is its upper half, so the model's 7.19 %/yr passes against a target set at the fast end of what is quoted. AUDITED AT v2.13. BAND CHECKED AT v2.22 AND DELIBERATELY LEFT NARROWER THAN THE SOURCE. Parfitt quotes 3-10 %/yr for cortical bone; ours is 5-10, the upper half. Unlike V5 and V16 this is narrower than the source, not looser, so it cannot produce a false pass - but it can produce a false fail, and it does exclude site-matched measurements: radiocarbon estimates give femoral cortex 3.3 %/yr and tibial cortex 3.7-5.0 %/yr, all of which our band would reject. Our 7.03 %/yr sits above every one of those. Left as is because a stricter band is the safe direction, but a model revision that lowered turnover towards 4 %/yr would be failed by our band while agreeing with the measurements.

phenomenon: Bone loss under bed rest or weightlessness (hip, lumbar spine)
notes: Source: BMD declines 1-2 %/month at weight-bearing sites over 90 days of head-down bed rest (Spatz 2012, PMID 22767636). NOTE ON UNITS: the column name says dBMD_per_month but evalTargets computes the change in bone mineral CONTENT. In disuse the periosteum barely moves (-0.002 mm over 180 days) and the two agree to 0.003 percentage points per month, so the label is inaccurate rather than the number; under loading the same two measures differ by 59 %. AUDITED AT v2.13. BAND CHECKED AT v2.22 AND LEFT NARROWER THAN THE SOURCE. Spatz reports 1-2 %/month; ours is 1.0-1.5, tighter at the top. The LOWER bound, which is the one that binds in practice, is the source's own. That matters for P5n: adopting Lerebours's measured specific-surface exponent drives V2 to 0.944 %/month, which fails 1.0-2.0 just as it fails 1.0-1.5. The P5n failure is therefore NOT an artefact of a self-set band - it fails against the source's own range, so widening the band is not an escape route.

Direction must be an increase. AUDITED AT v2.13 - MET in direction, PARTLY MET in shape. Source: Spatz 2012 (PMID 22767636) measured serum sclerostin over 90 days of head-down bed rest at +29 % (day 28), +42 % (day 60, peak) and +22 % (day 90). The model reaches +48.8 % by day 28 and stays flat: the rise and roughly the peak magnitude are reproduced, the attenuation is not, because sclerostin here equilibrates within days to the new mechanical dose. THE SAME EXPERIMENT ALSO FAILS AN UNTESTED CHECK: Spatz reports PTH falling 17 % (day 28) and 24 % (day 60) with urinary calcium elevated throughout, the classic immobilisation picture. The model gives serum calcium +0.006 % and PTH -0.01 %, because phi_res and phi_form are 0.10 while the flux imbalance is normalised by a baseline intestinal absorption over a thousand times larger - so the bone-to-blood arm of the systemic coupling is numerically negligible. See appendix C26.

36 cycles already suffice to trigger an osteogenic response; marginal return falls monotonically across 36, 216 and 1200 cycles. From v1.4 this emerges from accumulation in the inactivated channel state rather than being fitted.

Conditional: substantial amplification at low amplitude, fading as amplitude rises. A single parameter set must satisfy both the positive and the negative case. TARGET CORRECTED AT v2.15 FROM THE FULL TEXT (Srinivasan 2002, PMID 12211431, Reference/a07.pdf): the 2-5 fold band used until now was OUR OWN INVENTION, never the source's. Srinivasan measured labelled periosteal surface in the avian ulna at 820-830 microstrain and reports 21.9 % with rest insertion against 3.8 % without, a 5.8-FOLD increase. The model gives 13.99-fold, so it still overshoots, but by 2.4x the reported value rather than by 2.8x an invented ceiling.
The mechanostat response should scale with ln(f) over 1-10 Hz. During calibration, alpha and f_c must be pinned offline and excluded from fitting.

notes: Tai 2015. The PLATEAU SHAPE is a hard requirement: the increment is reached within the first year and does not accumulate over the following eighteen months. From v1.3, with the loop closed, this should be emergent rather than fitted.

Raising the serum calcium set point must NOT raise bone mineral density. EVALUATED AT v2.13 (E7) - NOT MET: clamping serum calcium 2% above baseline at fixed intake raises 24-month areal density by +0.124%, which is the wrong sign. The magnitude is an order of magnitude below the loading response, so the permissive-versus-instructive contrast of P1 survives, but the sign does not match the Mendelian randomisation evidence. Related defect found by the same run: dietary intake of 400 versus 1500 mg/day moves serum ionised calcium from 1.107 to 1.291 mmol/L, a 15% spread, whereas physiological serum calcium is defended within about 2%. Passive intestinal absorption is linear and unsaturating in intake, so it dominates the saturating active term, and the saturable tubular reabsorption that renal_k and renal_Ca_th were declared for is never implemented in code.

phenomenon: Romosozumab lumbar spine BMD at 12 months
notes: Romosozumab lumbar spine BMD at 12 months. BAND CORRECTED AT v2.22 TO THE PUBLISHED CONFIDENCE INTERVAL (Cosman 2016, FRAME, Reference/a09.pdf): 'at 12 months the percentage change from baseline was greater with romosozumab than with placebo at the lumbar spine, by 13.3 percentage points (95% CI, 11.9 to 14.7)'. Our band had been 11-14, shifted down about 0.8 points from the actual interval - traceable to the real number but not equal to it. Unlike V5, tau_target and V16, this self-set band was nearly right, and the model passes either way (V8 = 12.04). ONE MISMATCH REMAINS AND IS NOT FIXED HERE: Cosman's 13.3 is the PLACEBO-SUBTRACTED difference, whereas evalTargets computes the raw change from baseline in the treated arm. Both control arms are near-flat - ours drifts -0.019 % over 24 months - so the two are close in practice, but they are not the same quantity, and the comparison should eventually be made like for like.
The formation marker falls back after 6-12 months.
Substantial loss within 12 months. HOLD-OUT; does not enter calibration.

Ratio greater than 3. From v1.3 this arises from the resorption-state mechanism of the specific-surface function S_v(f_bm). EVALUATED AT v2.13 (E7) - MET: after 180 days of unloading, half the loss accrues in 139 days but takes 3582 days to win back on reambulation, a ratio of 25.8, and ten years recovers only 51.5% of it. NOTE: this is a rate asymmetry, NOT evidence of bistability - recovery is monotone and continuing, consistent with the falsification of P3.
Loading is additive or synergistic with anabolic agents (PTH, sclerostin antibody), but not with bisphosphonates.

Exogenous sclerostin raises RANKL and lowers OPG. TARGET CORRECTED AT v2.15 FROM THE FULL TEXT (Wijenayaka 2011, PMID 21991382, Reference/a02.pdf). The 'about 7-fold' figure is OSTEOCLASTIC RESORPTION - pit area in a 14-day osteocyte/splenocyte co-culture at 100 ng/ml rhSCL - NOT the instantaneous RANKL/OPG activation term that evalTargets and E7 were comparing it against. That was a wrong-contrast comparison on our side, of exactly the kind this audit exists to catch. The directly comparable molecular quantity is the RANKL:OPG ratio, which the paper reports rising dose-dependently; the model raises it 2.9-fold (RANKL 1.00 to 1.29, OPG 1.00 to 0.44). The 1.42-fold ceiling on the activation term pi_L is real arithmetic but answers a question the source never asked. Re-specifying this target against resorption output rather than pi_L is outstanding work.

Added at v1.3 as a zero-cost target: the emergent epsilon* should fall inside Frost's lazy zone. TIGHTENED AT v2.12 to follow the source: Frost 1987 (PMID 3688455) gives TWO SEPARATE thresholds - modelling adds bone at or above 1500-3000 microstrain, remodelling removes it below 100-300 microstrain. The lazy zone is strictly the interval between them, so the target was changed from 100-1500 to 300-1500; the former lower bound of 100 was the bottom of the remodelling range and made the target too permissive. The emergent value of 761.8 microstrain still passes after tightening. HOLD-OUT.

phenomenon: Geometric signature of the postmenopausal phenotype
notes: After oestrogen falls, the periosteal radius should expand slowly while the endocortical radius expands faster (the cortex thins and the bone widens). Both directions must be correct simultaneously. EVALUATED AT v2.13 (E7) - NOT MET: at E2 = 0.1 the run leaves the linear-elastic domain on day 334, so the phenotype is read at day 300. Inside the valid domain the endocortical radius expands (+0.0585 mm) and the cortex thins (-0.0607 mm) as required, but the periosteal radius drifts slightly INWARD (-0.0022 mm) instead of outward, so the bone does not widen and the target fails on its second half. A ten-year run appears to pass spectacularly (+5.75 mm of periosteal expansion) but lies entirely outside the elastic domain and is the same class of artefact that the modelling saturation bound was introduced to remove; it must not be reported.

After romosozumab withdrawal, CTX rises above baseline. THE 1.2-1.4 BAND IS OURS, NOT THE LITERATURE'S - established at v2.22 and it matters more here than elsewhere. The only source we cite for it, McClung 2018 (PMID 21991382... corrected: 29694685), states that after transition to placebo 'beta-CTX increased above baseline' - a DIRECTION, with no magnitude. We do not hold its full text. Cosman 2016 (FRAME, Reference/a09.pdf) cannot supply the number either: patients there transitioned to DENOSUMAB rather than placebo, so CTX is suppressed further rather than rebounding, and the phrase 'above baseline' does not occur in the paper at all. So the sourced content of this target is only ratio > 1.0, which the model satisfies at 1.183. TWO CONSEQUENCES. (1) V16 is a CALIBRATION target - sost_reb was fitted to it - so a self-set band was steering a fitted parameter. (2) The manuscript reports V16 as FAILING at 1.183 against 1.2-1.4; on this reading it fails an invented band while meeting the only thing the source actually says. The V7/V16 structural conflict (C27.5) is unaffected and remains real, since it concerns the sign of lambda_P's effect, not the band. Obtaining McClung's full text is the way to settle the magnitude.
